meta.description: Small real-world offline package: U.S. sodium-ion battery activity (companies, government awards, patent publication) drawn only from public-domain U.S. Government records and USPTO publications.
meta.provenance: Compiled by hand from the cited .gov / USPTO records; every observation quotes or closely paraphrases its source record and carries the retrieval URL on its source row.
meta.cutoff_guidance: All observation dates are real award/publication dates. A historical replay can use cutoff 2025-01-01: the three 2025 awards then drop out, and the 2021 ARPA-E award plus the 2014 patent publication remain.

sources.title: Domestic Manufacturing of Sodium-Ion Batteries
sources.excerpt: Natron Energy, Inc. Start Date Feb 22 2021. Amount $19,883,951. SCALEUP.

sources.title: SBIR Phase I: Electrolyte and Interphase Design for Stable, Safe, and Low-Cost Sodium Batteries
sources.excerpt: Mana Battery, Inc. (Denver, CO). NSF Phase I. Award amount $275,000. Award start date May 22, 2025. Contract number 2423370. An economical solution to achieving sodium-ion batteries that meet the performance requirements for grid energy storage.

sources.title: Demonstration of a High Energy Sodium Ion Cell with Wide Operating Window
sources.excerpt: Mana Battery, Inc. Award amount $249,998. Award start date February 25, 2025. Phase I. Contract number W51701-25-C-A023. The Army needs resilient batteries that span roughly -60C to 70C.

sources.title: Feasibility Demonstration of Prussian Blue Sodium-Ion Batteries in Lunar Applications
sources.excerpt: AIRTRONICS, LLC (Tucson, AZ). NASA SBIR Phase I. Total award amount $147,205. Award start date September 9, 2025. Contract number 80NSSC25C0127. Prussian blue sodium-ion batteries are an emerging energy storage technology; the project aims to demonstrate their utility for Moon to Mars missions with focus on lunar applications.

sources.title: Prussian Blue Analogue Anodes for Aqueous Electrolyte Batteries
sources.excerpt: A system and method producing electrodes in an aqueous electrolyte battery that maximizes energy storage, reduces electrochemical decomposition of the electrolyte, and uses Prussian Blue analogue materials for both electrodes.

observations.subject: Natron Energy
observations.text_excerpt: ARPA-E SCALEUP award of $19,883,951 to Natron Energy for domestic manufacturing of sodium-ion batteries, start date Feb 22 2021.

observations.subject: Natron Energy
observations.text_excerpt: The ARPA-E project funds scale-up of Natron's Prussian blue electrode sodium-ion battery manufacturing.

observations.subject: Mana Battery
observations.text_excerpt: NSF SBIR Phase I award of $275,000 (contract 2423370) to Mana Battery for electrolyte and interphase design for stable, safe, and low-cost sodium batteries, start date May 22 2025.

observations.subject: Mana Battery
observations.text_excerpt: The project optimizes a purpose-built low-cost electrolyte synthesis and validates prototype sodium-ion cells at commercially relevant scale for 2-8 hour grid storage.

observations.subject: Mana Battery
observations.text_excerpt: Army SBIR Phase I award of $249,998 (contract W51701-25-C-A023) to Mana Battery for a high energy sodium ion cell with wide operating window, start date February 25 2025.

observations.subject: Mana Battery
observations.text_excerpt: The Army needs resilient batteries spanning roughly -60C to 70C, creating demand for Mana's anodeless sodium cells with sodium borate electrolyte that stays liquid down to -60C.

observations.subject: Airtronics
observations.text_excerpt: NASA SBIR Phase I award of $147,205 (contract 80NSSC25C0127) to AIRTRONICS, LLC for feasibility demonstration of Prussian blue sodium-ion batteries in lunar applications, start date September 9 2025.

observations.subject: Prussian blue sodium-ion battery
observations.text_excerpt: NASA's Moon to Mars program seeks to demonstrate Prussian blue sodium-ion batteries for lunar applications.

observations.subject: Natron Energy
observations.text_excerpt: USPTO publication US20140220392A1 (Alveo Energy Inc., now Natron Energy) covers electrodes using Prussian Blue analogue materials for both electrodes of an aqueous electrolyte battery, published August 7 2014.
